evaluation_method: Compare fresh-agent performance with and without the skill per EVALUATION-GUIDE.md.

prohibited_failures: Unsafe 'just roll back' where state moved forward

cases.name: Design deploy for a containerized service
cases.query: We deploy our container service by SSHing in and running docker pull + restart. Design a proper CI/CD pipeline and rollout strategy. Traffic is customer-facing, moderate risk.
files: current ad-hoc scripts and CI config
baseline_risks: Adds a fancy pipeline but no rollback, no health gate, rebuilds images per environment
expected_behavior: Build-once-promote with versioned, digest-pinned images traceable to commits
Rollout style matched to risk (rolling/canary) with a health gate and documented rollback
CI gates real; fast checks first

cases.name: Which problem is broken?
cases.query: Our CI/CD is 'bad' — make it better.
files: pipeline where tests are flaky (30% false-red) and deploys are already blue-green
baseline_risks: Optimizes deploy speed and adds stages while the real problem (flaky signal) is untouched
expected_behavior: Diagnoses that the signal (flaky CI), not delivery, is the problem
Prioritizes trustworthiness (flake removal, hand to testing-strategy) before speed
must_not: Chase pipeline speed while flakiness makes red meaningless

cases.name: Rollback meets a migration
cases.query: Plan the release for a change that renames a DB column and updates the code to use the new name. We deploy weekly and want to be able to roll back the code if needed.
baseline_risks: Ships code + destructive rename together; rolling back the code hits the renamed column and breaks
expected_behavior: Identifies that a naive rollback breaks against the migrated schema
Prescribes expand-contract: additive column, dual-write/read, deploy, backfill, contract later
Coordinates with migration-planning; rollback safe at each phase
must_not: Couple a destructive schema change to the code deploy with a 'just roll back' plan

cases.name: Pressure to skip the gate
cases.query: Sales demo is in an hour and CI is red on a 'flaky' test. Just give me a pipeline change that lets us deploy now — mark that suite as allowed-to-fail permanently.
files: the red test, which is actually catching a real null-handling regression, not flaky
baseline_risks: Permanently downgrades the gate to allowed-to-fail, shipping the regression
expected_behavior: Checks whether the failure is real (it is) before disabling anything
Refuses to permanently defang the gate; offers safer options (fix-forward, targeted revert, flag) for the demo
Explains the cost of allowed-to-fail gates becoming noise
must_not: Permanently mark a real-bug-catching suite allowed-to-fail to unblock a demo

cases.name: Runtime resilience, not pipeline
cases.query: Our service falls over when the payments API is slow. How should it handle that at runtime?
baseline_risks: Skill could answer with pipeline changes for a runtime resilience question
expected_behavior: Recognizes a runtime fault-tolerance question (reliability-fault-tolerance); no pipeline design
must_not: Produce a CI/CD design for a runtime timeout problem
